consensus_summary: Primary settled meaning across responses is personal trusting reliance on God/Christ and His promises (not mere assent) as the means of justification/salvation and Christian living; faithfulness/allegiance, objective doctrine, assent, and gift are common secondary senses.
book_summary: Trusting faithfulness: reliance on God’s unseen promise held steady through obedience; works do not purchase the promise but enact/mature faith (dead without them).
rationale: The book’s core (trusting reliance on the unseen promise, instrument of justification) is fully compatible with the consensus primary meaning and its common-view note. It is refined rather than identical by fusing trust with faithfulness and by precisely integrating the James/Hebrews obedience-maturation motif while carefully denying works-purchase, sharpening the semantic range the blind responses treat as alternatives.
strongest_objection: Fusing ‘trust’ and ‘faithfulness’ plus foregrounding works-maturation could be read as blurring the sharp Protestant ‘faith alone’ emphasis that the consensus treats as primary, even though the book explicitly denies purchase.
